I've been working this land for 13 years. I know what works here in Quzhou. The soil is decent, my well pump is reliable, and I know the input costs and what prices I can expect at harvest. Some of my family members pull in wages off-farm, so I can't always count on their labor during peak times. I manage as efficiently as I can.

**Wheat (planted this October, harvested next June):**
My whole 5 mu goes into wheat first. I'll use an improved variety — probably Jimai 22 or whatever the county agricultural station is pushing this year that's locally adapted. Nothing fancy. I'll rotary-till after the maize is off in September, apply base fertilizer, then seed. I do three irrigations: the winter water in November to help it overwinter, jointing water in April, and a grain-filling irrigation in May. Fertilizer-wise, I put base phosphorus and potassium down at planting, split the nitrogen between base and a topdress at jointing. I spray herbicide in early spring and watch for powdery mildew and aphids — usually two or three pesticide runs total. I expect around 460 kg/mu if the weather cooperates.

**Maize (planted right after wheat harvest in June):**
Same 5 mu, back-to-back. I'll drill hybrid seed directly into the stubble — no-till saves me time and my son isn't always around to help. Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335, the hybrids I know perform here. Summer rains carry a lot of the water need, but I'll irrigate once or twice if we hit a dry spell at silking or grain fill. I put more nitrogen on maize than wheat — it needs it. Base fertilizer at planting, then a topdress at the big bell stage. One or two pesticide applications for corn borer and leaf diseases. I'm shooting for 570 kg/mu.
